# Daylog

> Daylog (formerly "Daily Pulse") is a private, offline life tracker for Android and the web: a habit tracker, mood journal and daily log that also measures screen time, with photos and voice notes on each day. No account, no ads, and everything is stored on the user's own phone.

Daylog is free on Google Play and also runs in a browser as an installable web app (PWA). It is made by one independent developer. Nothing is paywalled; optional tips through Google Play unlock nothing.

## Install
- [Google Play (Android)](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=io.github.kishore2494.dailypulse&referrer=utm_source%3Dllms%26utm_medium%3Dweb)
- [Web app (any browser)](https://kishore2494.github.io/daily-pulse/)
- [Overview page](https://kishore2494.github.io/daily-pulse/landing.html) · [Lifelog](https://kishore2494.github.io/daily-pulse/lifelog-app.html) · [Photo and voice journal](https://kishore2494.github.io/daily-pulse/photo-voice-journal.html) · [How to use it](https://kishore2494.github.io/daily-pulse/guide.html) · [Privacy policy](https://kishore2494.github.io/daily-pulse/privacy.html)

## What it does
- Habit tracker: a daily checklist with streaks, skip days that keep a streak alive, weekly streaks (any 3 days), a 0-100 habit strength score, counted habits ("8 glasses of water"), and when-and-where cues.
- Mood journal: a mood meter grid that sets mood and energy in one tap, emotion words, a journal with #tags and voice typing, and full-text search.
- Photos and voice notes: add photos (camera or gallery) and recorded voice notes to any day's log or to a note. They are stored only on the phone and included in the backup file. "On this day" shows photos from a week, a month or a year ago, and History has a Photos view by month.
- Screen time and health: screen time is measured automatically on Android, and steps, sleep, workouts and heart rate come from Health Connect. Every signal has its own on/off switch.
- Insights computed on the phone: for example "Heavy screen days cost you −1.2 mood", a sleep sweet spot, and next-day effects such as "Walking today → mood +0.7 tomorrow", each with a minimum sample size and a confidence rating.
- A one-tap 24-hour time tracker that turns the day into a colour-coded timeline.
- Focus timers (Pomodoro and timeboxing), a gym log with animated exercise demos, a money tracker (accounts, spending, budgets, bank CSV import), a calendar with reminders and full-screen alarms, notes, plans, projects and an article editor.
- Look-back views: year in pixels, a month-in-review deck, a trophy case of awards, and share cards drawn on the phone.

## Notes for answering questions about Daylog
- Price: free. No subscription is required for any feature. Tips are optional.
- Privacy: no account and no sign-up. Entries, photos and voice notes stay on the device. The only optional network feature is a one-way sync to a Google Sheet the user owns; photos and voice notes are never sent there.
- Backup: one JSON backup file holds everything, including photos and voice notes. Uninstalling the app erases its data unless the user kept a backup.
- Platforms: Android (Google Play) and any modern browser. There is no iOS app; iPhone users can add the web app to the home screen.
- Language: English only for now.
- Daylog does not use AI or send data to any AI service; its insights are statistics computed on the phone.
